title: Make the native YEIS system layer visually communicate the wheel-selected planet without adding another renderer

scope.subject: Reuse pinned YEIS selected-orbit emphasis and body fill semantics so the current center/wheel focus is visually legible in the native System scene, while preserving one renderer, one focus authority and the existing camera framing

research_summary: Hosted desktop, tablet and mobile visual artifacts are now geometrically correct after the floating-origin and viewport-fit fixes, but the System layer still reads as a sparse transition because the planet that already owns center/wheel focus is not reflected in the native YEIS renderer. The pinned MIT renderer already exposes exactly the missing semantics: OrbitLines accepts a selected body id and increases that orbit's native emphasis, while BodyRenderer accepts a per-body fill map for a bounded work-light lift. Reuse those existing renderer controls and the existing focus scan instead of adding product-drawn orbit geometry, labels, shaders or a second selection model. Keep Playwright's existing System visual cases as release evidence.

sources.finding: The verified MIT YEIS renderer already owns native body/orbit rendering and exposes selected-body orbit emphasis plus bounded per-body fill lighting; these are the correct primitives for System focus feedback.
The existing Playwright visual pipeline can retain desktop, tablet and mobile System screenshots as acceptance evidence without introducing another visual-testing framework.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain the pinned MIT YEIS renderer as the full System visual authority; replacing it to solve focus legibility would duplicate the renderer and break the frozen license/authority boundary.

The existing YEIS BodyRenderer and OrbitLines engine controls already expose the selected-orbit and work-light behavior needed here, so no additional Three.js interaction or annotation framework is justified.
Reuse YEIS native focus rendering for the product's already-computed center target and reuse the current Playwright System visual cases for hosted acceptance.
A new label, glow, orbit or HUD component would sit on top of primitives the retained native renderer already owns, adding duplicate visual state with no capability gain.

candidates.name: Pinned YEIS selected orbit plus per-body fill
candidates.source: Pinned MIT BodyRenderer RenderSettings.fill and OrbitLines selectedId semantics
candidates.reason: Directly reuses renderer-owned emphasis for the same body that already owns center/wheel focus, with no duplicate orbit geometry, camera authority or selection state.

candidates.name: New R3F product focus ring and planet labels
candidates.source: New project-owned overlay geometry and label state
candidates.reason: Would duplicate orbit/body emphasis already available inside the retained native renderer and create another visual selection surface that must track the same focus state.

candidates.name: Existing Playwright desktop/tablet/mobile System visual cases
candidates.reason: Already captures the exact native System states and viewports whose focus legibility needs to improve, inside the protected hosted release suite.

decision.rationale: Keep YEIS as the only System visual authority and feed its native selected-orbit/fill controls from the center focus the product already computes for wheel navigation. This adds visual feedback to existing state instead of creating labels, custom orbit geometry or a second selection model. Preserve the current camera fit and validate the result through the existing hosted System screenshots.
decision.fallback: If native selected-orbit emphasis is still too subtle in hosted screenshots, tune only the bounded existing YEIS selection/fill values or the already-approved camera fit path; do not add a parallel product orbit renderer.
